decisions.reason: As a flagship product with uncertain but promising prospects in reusable agricultural packaging, it is a valuable option, and with one year of evidence it is too early to abandon.
A foldable large container line with its own page fits the core business and costs little to keep, so the option stays open while demand resolves.
Stackable crates are low-cost extensions of established tooling, and with only a brief mention so far there is no evidence yet justifying abandonment.
The rackable pallet line serves established pallet customers at low marginal cost, and its value is not yet resolved, so keeping the option is sensible.
The spill-retention pallet addresses a niche industrial need, has its own page, and is cheap to maintain while uncertainty about uptake persists.
The pallet with load retainers is a specialized variant with low holding cost and insufficient results to date, so dropping it would be premature.
